doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Changing membership of the Jerry Hey Horns
summary: Original members have retired or moved; Hey recounts meeting Larry Williams, Gary Grant and Bill Reichenbach and trying to keep the sound.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Is it tough for you over the years to, you want to send in the Jerry Hey Horns so does that mean that you have to get on the phone with all the members every time you get called for a recording session? To see that they could all make it?

Well you know Gary Grant is not playing anymore so you know he was like a key member of the horn section. Bill Reichenbach has moved to near Asheville, North Carolina, and he’s also another, was a key member. He comes back to play on movies now. He does all the John Williams’ movies and plays on movies but he’s not always here when I do a session. And Larry Williams, who is still playing saxophone but because of a lot of times it’s baritone saxophone now and Dan Higgins plays everything amazingly well so he’s kind of been the main guy. So I’ll call — I mean I call the guys who I think are best for the job and Wayne Bergeron is kind of the guy now who can play anything. So he plays. Andy Martin plays trombone and Dan Higgins. The second trumpet chair is kind of rotating I guess. Dan Fornero’s been playing a little bit and a couple of other guys play. Rashawn Ross, who plays with Dave Mathews — so you know it’s still called the Jerry Hey Horns although it’s not the same guys. But you know I’m doing the arranging and it still kind of sounds the same, not quite the same but close.
I’m sure it’s excellent, and it’s a blessing to have that group of musicians who you’d have to go out of your way to get someone who wasn’t cutting it.

Yes. Yeah, no, the guys can play anything that you’re going to write, and you know you just, for me I have to kind of, because I’m not playing and we’re not playing with — so the guys in the original horn section, I went to Indiana with Larry Williams and Gary Grant, when we were living in Hawaii Gary Grant came over to Hawaii and we were together in Hawaii before we were in L.A. for four years we were in Hawaii before that. So we’ve known each other for 52 years, Gary. Larry Williams has been 55 years, and Bill Reichenbach I met on one session here when we were first in town in 1976. So you know it’s hard to get that team who played together for 40 years, and now you’ve got new guys coming in who don’t have that team playing together thing that I kind of have to, okay this is how I want that phrased, and this is how I really want that to sound. And it’s not necessarily like they would play it if I wasn’t there. So I’m still trying to put my influence on the tunes.
